quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: on time vs in time
quests.question: Despite the traffic, she still managed to arrive ___ for her interview.
quests.targetSentence: Despite the traffic, she still managed to arrive on time for her interview.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: on time vs in time
quests.ruleExplanation: 'On time' describes punctuality — arriving exactly when scheduled, not simply before a limit.
quests.nativeTip: This describes being punctual, exactly when expected.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'on time' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Despite the traffic, she still managed to arrive on time for her interview.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: on time vs in time
quests.question: We got to the station just ___ to catch the last train.
quests.targetSentence: We got to the station just in time to catch the last train.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: on time vs in time
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In time' describes having enough time to do something before a deadline or limit, unlike 'on time', which describes exact punctuality.
quests.nativeTip: This describes having just enough time to spare before a limit, not exact punctuality.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in time' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'We got to the station just in time to catch the last train.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: on time vs in time
quests.question: The ambulance arrived ___ to save his life, but only just.
quests.targetSentence: The ambulance arrived in time to save his life, but only just.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: on time vs in time
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In time' fits again here, emphasizing a narrow margin before a critical moment, the same pattern as the earlier train example.
quests.nativeTip: This emphasizes a narrow margin before it would have been too late, not a scheduled arrival.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in time' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The ambulance arrived in time to save his life, but only just.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: at the end vs in the end
quests.question: There's a summary ___ the chapter that reviews the key points.
quests.targetSentence: There's a summary at the end the chapter that reviews the key points.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: at the end vs in the end
quests.ruleExplanation: 'At the end of' refers to a specific location, such as the final section of a chapter.
quests.nativeTip: This refers to a specific physical location within a text, not an eventual outcome.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'at the end' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'There's a summary at the end the chapter that reviews the key points.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: at the end vs in the end
quests.question: We argued about it for hours, but ___ we agreed to compromise.
quests.targetSentence: We argued about it for hours, but in the end we agreed to compromise.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: at the end vs in the end
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In the end' means 'eventually' or 'after everything considered', describing an outcome rather than a location.
quests.nativeTip: This describes an eventual outcome after a long process, not a physical location.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in the end' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'We argued about it for hours, but in the end we agreed to compromise.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: at the end vs in the end
quests.question: By the final page, the hero realizes, ___, that the treasure was never really about gold.
quests.targetSentence: By the final page, the hero realizes, in the end, that the treasure was never really about gold.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: at the end vs in the end
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In the end' fits the idea of an eventual realization, distinct from a literal position like 'at the end of the book'.
quests.nativeTip: This describes the eventual moral of the story, not a literal position in the text.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in the end' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'By the final page, the hero realizes, in the end, that the treasure was never really about gold.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: on foot vs by + vehicle
quests.question: It's faster to get there ___ than to wait for a bus.
quests.targetSentence: It's faster to get there on foot than to wait for a bus.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: on foot vs by + vehicle
quests.ruleExplanation: 'On foot' is the standard fixed phrase for walking somewhere, an exception to the usual 'by + vehicle' pattern.
quests.nativeTip: This is the standard fixed phrase for walking as a means of transport.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'on foot' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'It's faster to get there on foot than to wait for a bus.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: on foot vs by + vehicle
quests.question: They decided to travel ___ train instead of flying, to enjoy the scenery.
quests.targetSentence: They decided to travel by train instead of flying, to enjoy the scenery.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: on foot vs by + vehicle
quests.ruleExplanation: 'By' is used for methods of transport, without an article before the noun, unlike the special exception for walking.
quests.nativeTip: This is the standard word for naming a method of transport, used without an article.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'by' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'They decided to travel by train instead of flying, to enjoy the scenery.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: on foot vs by + vehicle
quests.question: Rather than driving, we walked the last mile ___, enjoying the fresh air.
quests.targetSentence: Rather than driving, we walked the last mile on foot, enjoying the fresh air.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: on foot vs by + vehicle
quests.ruleExplanation: 'On foot' returns here, the same fixed exception taught earlier in this level.
quests.nativeTip: This is the fixed phrase from the earlier example, describing walking as the method of movement.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'on foot' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Rather than driving, we walked the last mile on foot, enjoying the fresh air.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: in control vs under control
quests.question: After a tense hour, the fire was finally brought ___ by the firefighters.
quests.targetSentence: After a tense hour, the fire was finally brought under control by the firefighters.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: in control vs under control
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Under control' describes a situation being successfully managed, without naming an active agent directing it.
quests.nativeTip: This describes a situation being managed, without naming who is actively directing it.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'under control' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'After a tense hour, the fire was finally brought under control by the firefighters.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: in control vs under control
quests.question: As the new manager, she felt confident and fully ___ the situation.
quests.targetSentence: As the new manager, she felt confident and fully in control of the situation.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: in control vs under control
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In control of' names an active person directing a situation, unlike 'under control', which describes the situation itself without naming an agent.
quests.nativeTip: This names a specific person actively directing things, unlike the passive phrase used for situations.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in control of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'As the new manager, she felt confident and fully in control of the situation.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: in control vs under control
quests.question: The pilot remained calm, staying ___ the aircraft even as the storm intensified.
quests.targetSentence: The pilot remained calm, staying in control of the aircraft even as the storm intensified.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: in control vs under control
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In control of' fits again, naming the pilot as the active agent managing the aircraft.
quests.nativeTip: An active person is directing something here, the same pattern as the manager example.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in control of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The pilot remained calm, staying in control of the aircraft even as the storm intensified.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: on purpose vs by accident

quests.targetSentence: I broke the vase by accident — it just slipped out of my hands.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: on purpose vs by accident
quests.ruleExplanation: 'By accident' describes something unintentional, matching the detail that it 'just slipped'.
quests.nativeTip: This describes something unintentional, not a deliberate action.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'by accident' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'I broke the vase by accident — it just slipped out of my hands.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: on purpose vs by accident
quests.question: He knocked over the chess board ___, just to annoy his little brother.
quests.targetSentence: He knocked over the chess board on purpose, just to annoy his little brother.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: on purpose vs by accident
quests.ruleExplanation: 'On purpose' describes a deliberate action, confirmed here by the stated motive to annoy his brother.
quests.nativeTip: This describes a deliberate action, confirmed by the stated motive.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'on purpose' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'He knocked over the chess board on purpose, just to annoy his little brother.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: on purpose vs by accident
quests.question: She claimed she'd deleted the file ___, but nobody believed her.
quests.targetSentence: She claimed she'd deleted the file by accident, but nobody believed her.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: on purpose vs by accident
quests.ruleExplanation: 'By accident' fits again, describing an unintentional action, the same phrase taught with the vase example.
quests.nativeTip: This is the same fixed phrase for something unintentional, taught earlier in this level.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'by accident' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'She claimed she'd deleted the file by accident, but nobody believed her.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: at random vs in order

quests.targetSentence: The judges selected three contestants at random to go first.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: at random vs in order

quests.nativeTip: This describes a selection with no particular pattern or sequence.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'at random' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The judges selected three contestants at random to go first.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: at random vs in order
quests.question: Please arrange the documents ___ before submitting them.
quests.targetSentence: Please arrange the documents in order before submitting them.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: at random vs in order
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In order' describes a deliberate, organized sequence, the opposite idea of 'at random'.
quests.nativeTip: This describes a deliberate, organized sequence, the opposite of the earlier example.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in order' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Please arrange the documents in order before submitting them.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: at random vs in order
quests.question: Names were drawn ___ from a hat to decide the speaking order.
quests.targetSentence: Names were drawn at random from a hat to decide the speaking order.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: at random vs in order
quests.ruleExplanation: 'At random' returns here, describing a selection made without a deliberate pattern.
quests.nativeTip: This is the same fixed phrase from the earlier example, describing an unpatterned selection.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'at random' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Names were drawn at random from a hat to decide the speaking order.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: for sale vs on sale
quests.question: The old farmhouse down the road has been ___ for almost a year now.
quests.targetSentence: The old farmhouse down the road has been for sale for almost a year now.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: for sale vs on sale
quests.ruleExplanation: 'For sale' means available to be purchased, distinct from 'on sale', which specifically means discounted.
quests.nativeTip: This simply describes being available to buy, not being discounted.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'for sale' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The old farmhouse down the road has been for sale for almost a year now.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: for sale vs on sale
quests.question: These winter coats are ___ this week only, thirty percent off.
quests.targetSentence: These winter coats are on sale this week only, thirty percent off.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: for sale vs on sale
quests.ruleExplanation: 'On sale' specifically means discounted, confirmed here by the mention of thirty percent off.
quests.nativeTip: This specifically describes a temporary price reduction.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'on sale' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'These winter coats are on sale this week only, thirty percent off.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: for sale vs on sale
quests.question: Is this necklace ___, or is it just part of the display?
quests.targetSentence: Is this necklace for sale, or is it just part of the display?
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: for sale vs on sale
quests.ruleExplanation: 'For sale' fits again here, simply asking whether an item is available for purchase.
quests.nativeTip: This asks whether an item is available to purchase at all, not whether it's discounted.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'for sale' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Is this necklace for sale, or is it just part of the display?'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: in stock vs out of stock
quests.question: Good news — the item you wanted is back ___.
quests.targetSentence: Good news — the item you wanted is back in stock.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: in stock vs out of stock
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In stock' means an item is currently available to purchase from inventory.
quests.nativeTip: This means an item is available again in the warehouse.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in stock' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Good news — the item you wanted is back in stock.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: in stock vs out of stock
quests.question: Unfortunately, that size is currently ___, but we expect more next week.
quests.targetSentence: Unfortunately, that size is currently out of stock, but we expect more next week.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: in stock vs out of stock
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Out of stock' means an item is temporarily unavailable, the opposite of 'in stock'.
quests.nativeTip: This means an item is temporarily unavailable, the opposite of the earlier example.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'out of stock' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Unfortunately, that size is currently out of stock, but we expect more next week.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: in stock vs out of stock
quests.question: Please let me know if the part is ___ before I drive all the way there.
quests.targetSentence: Please let me know if the part is in stock before I drive all the way there.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: in stock vs out of stock
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In stock' fits again, asking whether an item is currently available for purchase.
quests.nativeTip: This asks whether an item is currently available, following the earlier pattern.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in stock' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Please let me know if the part is in stock before I drive all the way there.'

quests.grammarRule: Contrast: at random vs in order

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: at the end vs in the end
quests.question: They decided, ___, that moving abroad had been the right decision after all, despite the early struggles.
quests.targetSentence: They decided, in the end, that moving abroad had been the right decision after all, despite the early struggles.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: at the end vs in the end

quests.nativeTip: This describes an eventual conclusion reached after a difficult process, not a literal location.

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: in control vs under control

quests.grammarRule: Contrast: in control vs under control
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Under control' fits here, describing a difficult situation being successfully managed overall.
quests.nativeTip: This describes a difficult situation eventually being managed, without naming a specific active agent.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'under control' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The negotiations remained tense, but the two sides eventually got things under control before the deadline passed.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: on purpose vs by accident
quests.question: Whether she said it ___ or simply misspoke, the comment caused quite a stir at the meeting.
quests.targetSentence: Whether she said it on purpose or simply misspoke, the comment caused quite a stir at the meeting.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: on purpose vs by accident
quests.ruleExplanation: 'On purpose' closes this unit, contrasted directly against 'misspoke' — a deliberate act versus an accidental one.
